claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes give rise to osteoblasts during skeletal development.
source: Hypertrophic chondrocytes give rise to osteoblasts during skeletal development; however, the process by which these non-mitotic cells make this transition is not well understood.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a premise for the study.

claim: The process by which hypertrophic chondrocytes transition to osteoblasts is not well understood.
source: Hypertrophic chondrocytes give rise to osteoblasts during skeletal development; however, the process by which these non-mitotic cells make this transition is not well understood.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the abstract.

claim: Skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) localize to the surrounding periosteum during skeletal development.
source: Prior studies have also suggested that skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) localize to the surrounding periosteum and serve as a major source of marrow-associated SSPCs, osteoblasts, osteocytes, and adipocytes during skeletal development.
evidence: This is cited as prior knowledge from other studies.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs serve as a major source of marrow-associated SSPCs, osteoblasts, osteocytes, and adipocytes during skeletal development.
source: Prior studies have also suggested that skeletal stem and progenitor cells (SSPCs) localize to the surrounding periosteum and serve as a major source of marrow-associated SSPCs, osteoblasts, osteocytes, and adipocytes during skeletal development.
evidence: This is cited as prior knowledge from other studies.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo a process of dedifferentiation to generate marrow-associated SSPCs.
source: Our data demonstrate that hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo a process of dedifferentiation to generate marrow-associated SSPCs that serve as a primary source of osteoblasts during skeletal development.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data from lineage tracing, scRNA-seq, and other assays.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs serve as a primary source of osteoblasts during skeletal development.
source: Our data demonstrate that hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo a process of dedifferentiation to generate marrow-associated SSPCs that serve as a primary source of osteoblasts during skeletal development.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract, supported by lineage tracing and scRNA-seq data.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs commit to a CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cell phenotype during skeletal development.
source: These hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs commit to a CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cell phenotype during skeletal development and demonstrate unique abilities to recruit vasculature and promote bone marrow establishment, while also contributing to the adipogenic lineage.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding supported by scRNA-seq data showing Cxcl12 expression.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs demonstrate unique abilities to recruit vasculature.
source: These hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs commit to a CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cell phenotype during skeletal development and demonstrate unique abilities to recruit vasculature and promote bone marrow establishment, while also contributing to the adipogenic lineage.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by gene ontology analysis and transplantation assays.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs promote bone marrow establishment.
source: These hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs commit to a CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cell phenotype during skeletal development and demonstrate unique abilities to recruit vasculature and promote bone marrow establishment, while also contributing to the adipogenic lineage.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by transplantation assays showing marrow formation.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs contribute to the adipogenic lineage.
source: These hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs commit to a CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cell phenotype during skeletal development and demonstrate unique abilities to recruit vasculature and promote bone marrow establishment, while also contributing to the adipogenic lineage.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence showing tdTOMATO+ adipocytes.

claim: Most skeletal elements arise from a cartilage template via the process of endochondral ossification.
source: Most skeletal elements arise from a cartilage template via the process of endochondral ossification (Long and Ornitz, 2013; Olsen et al., 2000; Ono et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: During skeletal development, mesenchymal stem and progenitor cells condense and differentiate to form chondrocytes.
source: During skeletal development, mesenchymal stem and progenitor cells condense and differentiate to form chondrocytes or cartilage cells (Hirao et al., 2006; Maes et al., 2012; Olsen et al., 2000; Spencer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Chondrocytes undergo rapid proliferation while depositing an extracellular matrix rich in type II collagen.
source: These chondrocytes undergo rapid proliferation while depositing an extracellular matrix (ECM) rich in type II collagen (COL2A1), forming the initial immature cartilage rudiments (Ono et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Chondrocytes localized nearest the center of each rudiment exit the cell cycle and undergo hypertrophic differentiation.
source: As cartilage growth proceeds, the chondrocytes localized nearest the center of each rudiment exit the cell cycle and undergo a process of maturation and hypertrophic differentiation (Capasso et al., 1984; Kong et al., 1993; Kwan et al., 1997; Long and Ornitz, 2013; Olsen et al., 2000; Ono et al., 2019; Reginato et al., 1986; Schmid and Conrad, 1982).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes are identified by their specific expression of type X collagen (COL10A1).
source: Hypertrophic chondrocytes, which are identified by their specific expression of type X collagen (COL10A1), are ultimately responsible for secreting additional proteins such as Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor alpha (VEGFα), Platelet Derived Growth Factor beta (PDGFβ), and Indian Hedgehog (IHH) among other factors to promote both vascular invasion and osteoblast differentiation of the surrounding perichondrial progenitors (Capasso et al., 1984; Kwan et al., 1997; Olsen et al., 2000; Reginato et al., 1986; Schmid and Conrad, 1982; St-Jacques et al., 1999; Zelzer et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes secrete VEGFα, PDGFβ, and IHH to promote vascular invasion and osteoblast differentiation.
source: Hypertrophic chondrocytes, which are identified by their specific expression of type X collagen (COL10A1), are ultimately responsible for secreting additional proteins such as Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor alpha (VEGFα), Platelet Derived Growth Factor beta (PDGFβ), and Indian Hedgehog (IHH) among other factors to promote both vascular invasion and osteoblast differentiation of the surrounding perichondrial progenitors (Capasso et al., 1984; Kwan et al., 1997; Olsen et al., 2000; Reginato et al., 1986; Schmid and Conrad, 1982; St-Jacques et al., 1999; Zelzer et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Vessels from the perichondrium invade the hypertrophic cartilage to establish the marrow cavity.
source: As vessels from the perichondrium invade the hypertrophic cartilage to establish the marrow cavity, newly formed osteoblasts and their progenitors are delivered by these vessels to the marrow space (Maes et al., 2010; Olsen et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Newly formed osteoblasts and their progenitors are delivered by vessels to the marrow space.
source: As vessels from the perichondrium invade the hypertrophic cartilage to establish the marrow cavity, newly formed osteoblasts and their progenitors are delivered by these vessels to the marrow space (Maes et al., 2010; Olsen et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Osteoblasts secrete a type I collagen-rich matrix that mineralizes to replace cartilage with bone.
source: There, osteoblasts secrete a type I collagen (COL1A1)-rich matrix that ultimately mineralizes to replace the cartilage with bone, while the hypertrophic cartilage is remodeled and reduced with age (Olsen et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from prior literature.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes are essential for establishment of the marrow cavity and bone formation.
source: Hypertrophic chondrocytes are essential for both establishment of the marrow cavity and bone formation; however, their precise fate and direct or indirect contribution to bone formation has been questioned (Tsang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The precise fate and contribution of hypertrophic chondrocytes to bone formation has been questioned.
source: Hypertrophic chondrocytes are essential for both establishment of the marrow cavity and bone formation; however, their precise fate and direct or indirect contribution to bone formation has been questioned (Tsang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap with citation.

claim: Genetic evidence suggests that hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo transdifferentiation to directly generate osteoblasts and osteocytes.
source: Recent genetic evidence suggests that hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo a process of transdifferentiation to directly generate osteoblasts and osteocytes that contribute to the formation of trabecular and endocortical bone (Park et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2014b; Yang et al., 2014a; Zhou et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as existing evidence.

claim: Col2a1 is expressed within perichondrial and marrow associated cell populations that give rise to osteoblast lineage cells.
source: Utilization of the constitutive and inducible Col2a1Cre/Col2a1CreERT2 mouse lines have complicated our understanding of this lineage by the fact that in addition to their expression in immature chondrocytes, Col2a1 and these genetic tools have been noted to be expressed within and/or label directly perichondrial and marrow associated cell populations known to give rise to osteoblast lineage cells (Hilton et al., 2007; Long et al., 2001).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as a complicating factor in lineage tracing.

claim: Yang et al., 2014a established an approach for low-dose tamoxifen delivery to drive recombination in clones of immature chondrocytes using Col2a1CreERT2.
source: Some of the more convincing data generated utilizing a Col2a1CreERT2 mouse line and recombination-sensitive reporter comes from Yang et al., 2014a, which established an approach for low-dose tamoxifen delivery to drive recombination in clones or clusters of immature chondrocytes that could be tracked over time.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature describing a specific methodology.

claim: With short chase periods (1-5 days), Col2a1CreERT2 reporter expression was restricted to immature chondrocyte clusters.
source: When the chase period was short (1–5 days post tamoxifen), reporter expression was largely restricted to immature chondrocyte clusters or extensions of these clusters into early hypertrophic chondrocytes.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Yang et al., 2014a) describing experimental results.

claim: With extended chase periods (10 days), Col2a1CreERT2 reporter expression extended into Col1a1-expressing osteoblasts.
source: However, when the chase period was extended (10 days post tamoxifen), reporter expression could be observed throughout individual columns of proliferating to hypertrophic chondrocytes that also extended into Col1a1-expressing osteoblasts localized only to the regions of metaphyseal bone directly underneath the labeled chondrocytes; a result that is consistent with chondrocytes transitioning to an osteoblastic fate (Yang et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Yang et al., 2014a) describing experimental results.

claim: AcanCreERT2 pulse-chase experiments showed reporter-positive non-chondrocytic cells in the primary spongiosa and trabecular bone.
source: Similar pulse-chase experiments were performed utilizing the AcanCreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato reporter model at both embryonic and adult time points utilizing doses of tamoxifen that elicit high rates of recombination in chondrocytes. These data suggested that following short (1–3 days post tamoxifen) or long (2 weeks post tamoxifen) chase periods, non-chondrocytic cells associated with the primary spongiosa and trabecular bone were reporter positive with some cells labeling with the Col1a1(2.3 kb)-eGFP.(Zhou et al., 2014b)
evidence: This is cited from prior literature (Zhou et al., 2014b) describing experimental results.

claim: Col10a1Cre/Col10a1CreERT2 mouse lines are more restricted in their expression to hypertrophic chondrocytes than Col2a1 or Acan-based lines.
source: The most convincing data was generated utilizing a combination of constitutive and inducible Col10a1Cre/Col10a1CreERT2 mouse lines and recombination-sensitive reporters; models that are much more restricted in their expression to hypertrophic chondrocytes of the growth plate (Yang et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is stated as an assessment of prior literature with citation.

claim: Studies using Col10a1Cre determined that hypertrophic chondrocytes give rise to osteoblastic cells expressing OSTERIX, COL1A1, OSTEOCALCIN, and SCLEROSTIN.
source: This study, as well as others solely utilizing a constitutive Col10a1Cre model, determined that hypertrophic chondrocytes can relatively quickly give rise to osteoblastic cells expressing OSTERIX (OSX), COL1A1, and eventually even OSTEOCALCIN (OCN) and/or SCLEROSTIN (SOST) expressing osteocytes within the trabecular and endocortical bone matrix (Park et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2014b; Yang et al., 2014a; Zhou et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature describing experimental results.

claim: Yang et al., 2014a observed YFP+, Perilipin-expressing adipocytes and YFP+, PDGFRβ+ pericytes in Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-eYFP bone marrow.
source: Interestingly, Yang et al., 2014a utilized a Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-eYFP reporter model and noted the presence of some YFP+, Perilipin-expressing adipocytes and YFP+, PDGFRβ+ pericytes within the bone marrow, suggesting the potential for alternate fates of hypertrophic chondrocytes beyond the osteoblast lineage.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature describing experimental observations.

claim: Tan et al., 2020 demonstrated that mature adipocytes can arise from Col10a1-expressing hypertrophic chondrocytes.
source: Utilizing similar techniques, Tan et al., 2020 also demonstrated the potential for mature adipocytes to arise from Col10a1-expressing hypertrophic chondrocytes.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature describing experimental results.

claim: At E16.5, hypertrophic chondrocytes and their tdTOMATO+ descendants were found within the newly formed bone marrow cavity in Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice.
source: These mice were harvested at E16.5 following tamoxifen injections from E13.5-E15.5. Hypertrophic chondrocytes and their descendants found within the newly formed bone marrow cavity were tdTOMATO+ (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Some tdTOMATO+ descendants co-expressed the osteoblast protein OCN at E16.5.
source: A number of these descendants co-expressed the osteoblast protein OCN (Figure 1b–c, white arrow); however, OCN-, tdTOMATO+ cells were also apparent within the marrow (Figure 1b–c, orange arrow).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1b-c.

claim: OCN-negative, tdTOMATO+ cells were present within the marrow at E16.5.
source: A number of these descendants co-expressed the osteoblast protein OCN (Figure 1b–c, white arrow); however, OCN-, tdTOMATO+ cells were also apparent within the marrow (Figure 1b–c, orange arrow).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1b-c.

claim: At 12 hours following tamoxifen administration at P6, tdTOMATO reporter was observed only within hypertrophic chondrocytes.
source: At 12 hr following TM administration, specific expression of the tdTOMATO reporter was observed within hypertrophic chondrocytes and no cells within the marrow or surrounding tissues (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: At 24 hours following tamoxifen administration at P6, tdTOMATO reporter was observed in marrow-associated cells directly below the cartilage growth plate.
source: At 24 hr following TM administration, the tdTOMATO reporter could now be observed in a limited number of marrow-associated cells directly below the cartilage growth plate, as well as within hypertrophic chondrocytes (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: At 2 weeks following tamoxifen administration at P6, tdTOMATO reporter had cleared from hypertrophic chondrocytes and was present in marrow-associated cells.
source: At 2 weeks following TM administration, the tdTOMATO reporter had cleared from the hypertrophic chondrocytes and was now exclusively present in a number marrow-associated cells; some of those being at a significant distance from the growth plate (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Trabecular bone lining cells co-labeled for tdTOMATO and OCN were observed 2 weeks after tamoxifen administration at P6.
source: In this distal region of the marrow, we also observed trabecular bone lining cells that co-labeled for tdTOMATO and OCN (Figure 1g; white arrows), suggesting that these cells had transitioned from hypertrophic chondrocytes to osteoblasts.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: tdTOMATO-positive, OCN-negative marrow-associated cells were observed 2 weeks after tamoxifen administration at P6.
source: Interestingly, other tdTOMATO-positive marrow-associated cells were not directly in contact with bone matrix and did not co-label with OCN (Figure 1g; orange arrow), suggesting the presence of another cell type or cell stage within the bone marrow that may be derived from hypertrophic chondrocytes.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes continue to contribute tdTOMATO+ cells to the bone marrow at 2 months and 4 months of age.
source: Additionally, by inducing recombination at both 2 months and 4 months of age and chasing for 2 and 4 weeks, respectively, we continued to observe contribution of tdTOMATO+ cells to the bone marrow (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, b).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a, b.

claim: In 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice, tdTOMATO reporter expression was observed in hypertrophic chondrocytes and osteogenic cells associated with trabecular and endocortical bone.
source: While tdTOMATO reporter expression was observed within hypertrophic chondrocytes and osteogenic cells associated with trabecular and endocortical bone of mice at P0 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d-f) and 2 months (2 M) of age (Figure 1h–j), CRE recombinase could only be detected within hypertrophic chondrocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1h-j.

claim: CRE recombinase was only detected within hypertrophic chondrocytes in Col10a1Cre mice.
source: While tdTOMATO reporter expression was observed within hypertrophic chondrocytes and osteogenic cells associated with trabecular and endocortical bone of mice at P0 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d-f) and 2 months (2 M) of age (Figure 1h–j), CRE recombinase could only be detected within hypertrophic chondrocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claim: 69.4% ± 14.8% of osteocytes were tdTOMATO reporter positive in 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice.
source: The vast majority of the trabecular and endocortical bone was lined with tdTOMATO reporter-positive cells, and 69.4% ± 14.8% of osteocytes were reporter positive (Figure 1k and l – white arrows).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1k and l.

claim: 83.3% ± 9.7% of all OCN-positive osteoblasts were tdTOMATO reporter positive in 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice.
source: We also observed that 83.3% ± 9.7% of all OCN-positive osteoblasts were tdTOMATO reporter positive, confirming that hypertrophic chondrocytes can give rise to the majority of intramedullary osteoblasts during bone development (Figure 1k and l – green arrows).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1k and l.

claim: Some OCN-positive osteoblasts were tdTOMATO-negative, indicating an alternate source such as the perichondrium/periosteum.
source: Of note, a number of tdTOMATO negative and OCN positive cells were also identified lining portions of the trabecular and endocortical bone, indicating that some of these osteoblasts originate from an alternate source such as the perichondrium/periosteum (Figure 1k).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1k and inferred from the presence of unlabeled osteoblasts.

claim: tdTOMATO reporter expressing cells within the marrow were localized to vessel-like structures.
source: Finally, utilizing this model, we were able to confirm the existence of tdTOMATO reporter expressing cells within the marrow that were not associated with bone matrix (white arrow); many of which were localized to vessel-like structures (yellow arrow) (Figure 1j).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1j.

claim: Single cell RNA-sequencing of E16.5 Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato cells yielded eight distinct cell clusters.
source: Using the 10 x Genomics platform, we performed scRNA-seq and further analyzed 2,273 tdTOMATO reporter positive sorted cells following quality control processing and elimination of a small number of cells lacking tdTomato transcripts. We then performed a Seurat-based unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles from the tdTOMATO positive cells, which ultimately yielded eight distinct cell clusters (Figure 2a; see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq data and UMAP visualization shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Both Cre and Col10a1 transcripts were detected in a portion of E16.5 tdTOMATO+ cells, while some cells expressed tdTomato without Cre or Col10a1.
source: Initial observations demonstrated that both Cre and Col10a1 transcripts were detected in a portion of the cells, but we also observed cells expressing tdTomato without expression of either Cre or Col10a1, indicating the presence of both hypertrophic chondrocytes and their descendants within these clusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a, i).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a, i.

claim: Ihh and Col10a1 expressing chondrocytes were most notably present in clusters 1, 3, and 5 at E16.5.
source: Differential gene expression analysis revealed the presence of Ihh and Col10a1 expressing chondrocytes (most notably in clusters 1, 3, and 5), identifying cells in transition from pre-hypertrophy to hypertrophy (Figure 2b and i; St-Jacques et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2b and i.

claim: Col10a1 expression was most highly enriched in clusters 1-5 and 7 at E16.5.
source: Col10a1 expression was observed throughout many clusters; however was most highly enriched in clusters 1–5 and 7 (Figure 2c and i).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2c and i.

claim: Sox9 and Aggrecan were moderately expressed throughout all clusters but primarily enriched in clusters 1-5 at E16.5.
source: Moderate expression of Sox9 and Aggrecan were observed throughout all clusters, but primarily enriched in clusters 1–5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2b-c, i).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2b-c, i.

claim: Mmp13 reached highest expression in clusters 4, 5, and 6 at E16.5.
source: Mmp13, noted for its role in terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes, reached highest expression in clusters 4, 5, and 6 (Figure 3d and i).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 3d and i (note: text references Figure 3d but likely means Figure 2d based on context).

claim: Osteogenic genes Sp7, Clec11a, Col1a1, Bglap, Runx2, Spp1, Alpl, and Ibsp were most highly expressed in clusters 7 and 8 at E16.5.
source: The osteogenic genes, Sp7, Clec11a, Col1a1, Bglap, Runx2, Spp1, Alpl, and Ibsp, were most highly expressed in clusters 7 and 8, which represent two potential osteoblast clusters (Figure 2e–h and i and Figure 2—figure supplement 2d-i), while some were also detected at much lower levels in pre-hypertrophic/hypertrophic chondrocyte clusters.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2e-h and i and Figure 2—figure supplement 2d-i.

claim: SSPC-associated genes Pdgfra, Ly6a, Lepr, and Cxcl12 were expressed within clusters 4, 5, and 6 at E16.5.
source: Differential gene expression analysis also identified the SSPC-associated genes, Pdgfra, Ly6a (encoding SCA1), Lepr, Cxcl12, to be expressed within clusters 4, 5, and 6, with some expression in cluster 8 (Figure 3a–e).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 3a-e.

claim: Pdgfra, Ly6a, Lepr, and Cxcl12 genes identify SSPCs capable of becoming osteoblasts in vivo.
source: Each of these genes and/or their regulatory elements genetically identify SSPCs capable of becoming osteoblasts in vivo (Crisan et al., 2008; Morikawa et al., 2009; Omatsu et al., 2010; Worthley et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge.

claim: Adipoq expression was not observed in any clusters at E16.5.
source: We did not observe Adipoq expression in any clusters, another gene previously shown to be co-expressed with Lepr in some SSPC populations (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h-i; Zhong et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2h-i.

claim: Pseudotime analysis indicated a singular trajectory linking hypertrophic chondrocytes to osteoblasts via an intermediate SSPC-like population at E16.5.
source: To further understand the cluster hierarchy of these hypertrophic chondrocytes and their descendants, we performed pseudotime analysis of the scRNA-seq data. This analysis indicated a singular trajectory linking hypertrophic chondrocytes (clusters 1–5) to osteoblasts (clusters 7 and 8) by way of an intermediate SSPC-like population (cluster 6) (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is supported by Monocle three trajectory analysis shown in Figure 3f.

claim: tdTOMATO and PDGFRaH2B-GFP double positive cells were identified within the marrow space at E16.5, some of which were OCN+ and some OCN-.
source: To validate this transition of hypertrophic chondrocytes to a marrow-associated SSPC fate, we generated Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato; PDGFRaH2B-GFP mice and performed additional in vivo lineage-tracing analysis at E16.5. Fluorescent reporter analysis identified a number of tdTOMATO and PDGFRaH2B-GFP double positive cells within the marrow space that were either OCN+ or OCN- (Figure 3g–h), indicating that tdTOMATO+, GFP+, and OCN- cells likely represent a more primitive hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPC.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 3g-h.

claim: tdTOMATO+, PDGFRaH2B-GFP+, OCN- cells likely represent a more primitive hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPC.
source: Fluorescent reporter analysis identified a number of tdTOMATO and PDGFRaH2B-GFP double positive cells within the marrow space that were either OCN+ or OCN- (Figure 3g–h), indicating that tdTOMATO+, GFP+, and OCN- cells likely represent a more primitive hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPC.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3g-h.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes give rise to marrow-associated SSPCs expressing LEPR, PDGFRα, and PDGFRβ at 3 weeks of age.
source: To further validate that hypertrophic chondrocytes are capable of giving rise to marrow-associated SSPCs expressing Lepr, Pdgfra, and Pdgfrb in vivo throughout development, we performed IF co-labeling assays on bone sections from Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26-tdTomato f/+ mice at 3 W of age (TM delivered at P6). Co-labeling of cells with tdTOMATO fluorescence and antibodies for LEPR, PDGFRα, and PDGFRβ demonstrate that hypertrophic chondrocytes indeed give rise to marrow associated SSPCs during skeletal development (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Single cell RNA-sequencing of 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato marrow cells yielded five distinct cell clusters.
source: Using the 10 x Genomics platform, we performed scRNA-seq and further analyzed 1,066 tdTOMATO reporter positive sorted cells following quality control processing and elimination of any cells lacking tdTomato transcripts. Since neither Cre nor Col10a1 expression could be detected in any of these cells, they clearly represented descendants of Col10a1Cre-expressing hypertrophic chondrocytes. Finally, we performed a Seurat-based unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles from the tdTOMATO-positive cells, which ultimately yielded five distinct cell clusters (Figure 4a; see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq data and UMAP visualization shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Neither Cre nor Col10a1 expression was detected in 2-month-old marrow-derived tdTOMATO+ cells, indicating they are descendants of hypertrophic chondrocytes.
source: Since neither Cre nor Col10a1 expression could be detected in any of these cells, they clearly represented descendants of Col10a1Cre-expressing hypertrophic chondrocytes.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data.

claim: Cells in clusters 1 and 2 at 2 months expressed osteogenic genes including Mepe, Dmp1, Fam20c, Bglap, and Col1a1.
source: Differential gene expression analyses further demonstrated that cells associated with clusters 1 and 2 expressed several known osteogenic genes (Figure 4b–h). Many cells in cluster one expressed genes such as Mepe, Dmp1, and Fam20c (Figure 4b–d and h), known for their roles in osteocytes and/or the bone mineralization process (Robling and Bonewald, 2020; Sapir-Koren and Livshits, 2014). Some cells in cluster 2 also expressed Dmp1 and Fam20c; however, their expression was detected at much lower levels. Most cells in cluster two expressed other osteoblast associated genes, such as Bglap and Col1a1 (Figure 4e–f and h), critical components of the organic bone matrix.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4b-h.

claim: Sp7 (encoding OSTERIX) was expressed in clusters 1 and 2, and in a limited number of cells in clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months.
source: Expression analyses further determined that the master transcriptional regulator of osteoblast differentiation and known osteoprogenitor cell marker, Sp7 (encoding the protein OSTERIX) (Maes et al., 2010; Mizoguchi et al., 2014), not only exhibited expression within osteoblast clusters 1 and 2, but also within a limited number of cells associated with clusters 3, 4, and 5 (Figure 4g–h).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4g-h.

claim: Cells in clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months are not osteoblasts or osteoprogenitors, but may be more primitive cells or distinct cell types.
source: These data suggest that the majority of marrow-associated cells derived from the hypertrophic chondrocytes localized to clusters 3, 4, and 5 are not osteoblasts or osteoprogenitors, but rather may be more primitive cells within the osteoblast lineage or distinct cell types altogether.
evidence: This is inferred from the scRNA-seq gene expression patterns.

claim: Lepr, Grem1, Pdgfra, Cxcl12, and Pdgfrb were highly expressed within cells across clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months.
source: This analysis identified a number of genes utilized for identifying SSPC populations. Specifically, Lepr, Grem1, Pdgfra (but not Ly6a – SCA1), Cxcl12, and Pdgfrb were highly expressed within cells across all three clusters (Figure 5a–f and k).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5a-f and k.

claim: Ly6a (SCA1) was not expressed in clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months.
source: Specifically, Lepr, Grem1, Pdgfra (but not Ly6a – SCA1), Cxcl12, and Pdgfrb were highly expressed within cells across all three clusters (Figure 5a–f and k).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5a-f and k.

claim: 74.21% ± 13.92% of all tdTOMATO+ cells were LEPR+ in 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice.
source: Quantification of Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato for LEPR demonstrates that 74.21%±13.92% of all tdTOMATO+ cells were LEPR+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: 73.6% ± 2.83% of tdTOMATO+ cells were PDGFRa-GFP+ in 1-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato; PDGFRaH2B-GFP mice.
source: We additionally performed flow cytometry of marrow cells from Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato; PDGFRaH2B-GFP mice at 1 month of age and observed 73.6% ± 2.83% of tdTOMATO+ cells were PDGFRa-GFP+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: 64.33% ± 3.48% of tdTOMATO+ cells were PDGFRB+ in 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice.
source: At 2 M of age, flow cytometry of marrow cells from Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice demonstrated that 64.33% ± 3.48% of tdTOMATO+ cells were PDGFRB+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claim: 37.4% ± 6.2% of the total LEPR+ population were tdTOMATO+ in 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice.
source: and that 37.4% ± 6.2% of the total LEPR+ population were also tdTOMATO+ as per quantitation from stained bone sections (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1a.

claim: 26.93% ± 3.79% of all PDGFRaH2B-GFP+ cells were tdTOMATO reporter positive in Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato; PDGFRaH2B-GFP mice.
source: This was further corroborated by utilizing flow cytometry of marrow cells from Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato; PDGFRaH2B-GFP mice, which demonstrates that a similar 26.93%±3.79% of all PDGFRaH2B-GFP+ cells were also tdTOMATO reporter positive (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs constitute nearly 25-45% of all marrow SSPCs at 2 months of age and younger.
source: These data indicate that hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs constitute nearly 25–45% of all marrow SSPCs at these stages, and that a significant portion of the marrow-associated SSPCs are likely derived from other origins such as the perichondrium and/or periosteum in mice 2 months of age and younger.
evidence: This is inferred from the flow cytometry and immunofluorescence quantification data.

claim: A significant portion of marrow-associated SSPCs are derived from other origins such as the perichondrium and/or periosteum in mice 2 months of age and younger.
source: These data indicate that hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs constitute nearly 25–45% of all marrow SSPCs at these stages, and that a significant portion of the marrow-associated SSPCs are likely derived from other origins such as the perichondrium and/or periosteum in mice 2 months of age and younger.
evidence: This is inferred from the flow cytometry and immunofluorescence quantification data showing that not all SSPCs are tdTOMATO+.

claim: Itgav is enriched in SSPC clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months.
source: While we identified Itgav expression sporadically throughout cells of all clusters, it is enriched in the SSPC clusters 3, 4, and 5 (Figure 5g and k).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5g and k.

claim: Cd200 is broadly expressed across all clusters including osteoblasts at 2 months.
source: Our gene expression analyses observed broad expression of Cd200 across all clusters including the osteoblasts; however, Eng (encoding CD105) was more restricted to SSPC clusters 3, 4, 5 and enriched specifically within cluster 4 (Figure 5h–i and k).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5h-i and k.

claim: Eng (encoding CD105) is more restricted to SSPC clusters 3, 4, 5 and enriched specifically within cluster 4 at 2 months.
source: Our gene expression analyses observed broad expression of Cd200 across all clusters including the osteoblasts; however, Eng (encoding CD105) was more restricted to SSPC clusters 3, 4, 5 and enriched specifically within cluster 4 (Figure 5h–i and k).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5h-i and k.

claim: 128 of 953 SSPCs were Itgav+, Cd200+, Cd105- at 2 months.
source: When assessing the precise cellular overlap of these factors, we observed 128 of 953 SSPCs to be Itgav+, Cd200+, Cd105-.
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data analysis.

claim: The most primitive SSC population (Itgav+, Cd200+, Cd105-) was relatively evenly distributed among clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months.
source: While this most primitive SSC population exists among our SSPCs analyzed via scRNA-seq, they were relatively evenly distributed among cells within clusters 3, 4, and 5 (Figure 5g–I and k).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 5g-I and k.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo dedifferentiation to generate even the most primitive SSCs.
source: These data suggest that hypertrophic chondrocytes likely undergo a process of dedifferentiation to generate even the most primitive SSCs; however, these cells themselves may be heterogeneous due to the differential expression of genes that allow for their segregation into multiple distinct clusters within our Seurat analysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the scRNA-seq data showing presence of primitive SSC markers in hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived cells.

claim: tdTOMATO+ cells were directly adjacent to EMCN expressing endothelial cells in 2-month-old Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice.
source: To assess this directly, we performed immunofluorescent staining for ENDOMUCIN (EMCN) on bone sections of Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice at 2 months of age and identified a number of tdTOMATO+ reporter cells directly adjacent to EMCN expressing endothelial cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3a.

claim: SSPCs in clusters 3, 4, and 5 showed limited or no expression of pericyte and vascular smooth muscle cell markers (Acta2, Nes, Kcnj8, Rgs5, Cspg4, Mcam).
source: To ensure that these tdTOMATO+ cells were not pericytes or vascular smooth muscle cells (vSMCs), we assessed our differential gene expression data for genes that serve as common markers for these specific cell types, including Acta2, Nes, Kcnj8, Rgs5, Cspg4, and Mcam (Chasseigneaux et al., 2018; Yamazaki and Mukouyama, 2018). We observed limited or no gene expression for these markers in SSPCs of clusters 3, 4, or 5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3b-g).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3b-g.

claim: Monocle three pseudotime analysis indicated a continuous trajectory from clusters 4 and 5 through cluster 3 to osteoblast clusters 2 and 1 at 2 months.
source: To finally parse the relatedness or relationship between SSPC and osteoblast cell clusters, we performed Monocle three pseudotime cell trajectory analysis of the Seurat data. These data indicate a clear hierarchy of cellular differentiation and relatedness between all cell clusters in an unbranched or continuous trajectory. Clusters 4 and 5 shared a common trajectory, with cluster 4 being slightly earlier in pseudotime. These clusters then give rise to cluster 3, which further differentiates into the osteoblast clusters 2 and then 1 (Figure 5j).
evidence: This is supported by Monocle three trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5j.

claim: Clusters 3, 4, and 5 are hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs capable of becoming osteoblasts with unique niche localizations.
source: Taken together these data indicate that cluster 3, 4, and 5 are hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs that are capable of becoming osteoblasts and have unique niche localizations with at least some of these SSPCs being vessel associated.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined scRNA-seq, immunofluorescence, and trajectory analysis data.

claim: Runx2 is broadly and robustly expressed throughout all clusters and especially concentrated in SSPC clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months.
source: While we observed limited expression of the osteoprogenitor transcription factor Sp7 in the SSPC clusters 3, 4, and 5, we noticed much broader and robust expression of Runx2, the earliest master transcriptional regulator of osteoblast specification, throughout all clusters and especially concentrated in the SSPC clusters 3, 4, and 5 (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: RUNX2 primes cells for osteoblastic specification and differentiation.
source: RUNX2 has been observed in LEPR+ cells and appears to prime cells for osteoblastic specification and differentiation (Yang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge.

claim: Pparg and Adipoq are expressed within Lepr-expressing SSPCs of clusters 3, 4, and 5 at 2 months.
source: Recent data has shown that some LEPR+ SSPCs also express PPARγ (encoded by Pparg) and ADIPONECTIN (encoded by Adipoq) (Zhong et al., 2020). Similar to this report we observed Pparg and Adipoq expression within Lepr-expressing SSPCs of clusters 3, 4, and 5 (Figure 6b–c).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 6b-c.

claim: Perilipin (Plin1) was not detected in SSPC clusters 3, 4, or 5 at 2 months.
source: Our differential gene expression analysis did not indicate the presence of Perilipin (Plin1), a mature lipid laden adipocyte marker, in SSPC clusters 3, 4, or 5, suggesting that none of these cells isolated utilizing our procedures were representative of mature adipocytes (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice displayed co-localization of tdTOMATO reporter and PERILIPIN at 2 months and 13 months of age.
source: Providing evidence for an ultimate adipogenic fate for some of these SSPCs, Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice at 2months and 13months of age displayed co-localization of the tdTOMATO reporter and PERILIPIN antibody staining (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Approximately 25% of PERILIPIN-labeled adipocytes were tdTOMATO reporter positive at 13 months of age.
source: By 13 M of age, approximately 25% of adipocytes labeled with PERILIPIN were also tdTOMATO reporter positive (Figure 6f).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs are a significant contributor to the adipogenic fate.
source: Therefore, our results suggest that hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs are also a significant contributor to the adipogenic fate; however, these mature cells likely eluded our scRNA-seq analyses due to the technical nature for isolating and sorting lipid laden adipocytes and their limited availability in the bone marrow at 2 months of age.
evidence: This is inferred from the immunofluorescence data showing tdTOMATO+ adipocytes.

claim: At P0, LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice showed reporter positive marrow-associated and bone lining cells, but no OCN+, tdTOMATO+ osteoblasts.
source: Utilizing bone sections of P0 LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato reporter mice, we observed reporter positive signals in both-marrow-associated cells and some bone lining cells; however, OCN+, tdTOMATO+ osteoblasts were not apparent (Figure 4—figure supplement 4a).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4a.

claim: At 2 months, LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice showed OCN-expressing osteoblasts, osteocytes, and adipocytes that were tdTOMATO reporter positive.
source: By 2 M of age we observed bone lining cells, OCN-expressing osteoblasts, and osteocytes that were tdTOMATO reporter positive (Figure 4—figure supplement 4a – white arrows), similar to data previously reported (Zhou et al., 2014a). As expected, a limited number of PERILIPIN+, tdTOMATO+ adipocytes were also observed within the bone marrow of 2 M old LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 4a).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4a.

claim: At P0, AdipoqCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice showed marrow-associated and bone lining reporter-positive cells that had not yet contributed to OCN+ osteoblasts.
source: Similarly, P0 AdipoqCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato bone sections exhibited marrow-associated and bone lining reporter-positive cells that not yet contributed to OCN+ osteoblasts; however, by 2 M of age tdTOMATO+ and OCN+ osteoblasts were observed, as well as tdTOMATO+ osteocytes and adipocytes (PLIN1+) were apparent in Adipoq Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato bone sections (Figure 4—figure supplement 4b – white arrows).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4b.

claim: At 2 months, AdipoqCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice showed tdTOMATO+ OCN+ osteoblasts, osteocytes, and adipocytes.
source: Similarly, P0 AdipoqCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato bone sections exhibited marrow-associated and bone lining reporter-positive cells that not yet contributed to OCN+ osteoblasts; however, by 2 M of age tdTOMATO+ and OCN+ osteoblasts were observed, as well as tdTOMATO+ osteocytes and adipocytes (PLIN1+) were apparent in Adipoq Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato bone sections (Figure 4—figure supplement 4b – white arrows).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4b.

claim: Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato descendants demonstrate a relatively quick commitment to the osteoblast lineage observed at P0 and earlier.
source: In contrast with these studies, Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato descendants demonstrate a relatively quick commitment to the osteoblast lineage that is observed at P0 and earlier, while Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice document that bone lining cells and mature OCN-expressing osteoblasts can be generated from hypertrophic chondrocytes within 1 day to 2 weeks (Figure 1a–g).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1a-g.

claim: Bone lining cells and mature OCN-expressing osteoblasts can be generated from hypertrophic chondrocytes within 1 day to 2 weeks.
source: In contrast with these studies, Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato descendants demonstrate a relatively quick commitment to the osteoblast lineage that is observed at P0 and earlier, while Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice document that bone lining cells and mature OCN-expressing osteoblasts can be generated from hypertrophic chondrocytes within 1 day to 2 weeks (Figure 1a–g).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1a-g.

claim: There are functional differences between sub-populations of LEPR and ADIPOQ expressing SSPCs based on their origin and/or niche.
source: This highlights the potential for functional differences between sub-populations of LEPR and ADIPOQ expressing SSPCs based on their particular origin and/or niche.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of lineage tracing kinetics between different Cre lines.

claim: 50-60% of CFU-F colonies from Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice exhibited tdTOMATO reporter expression at 2 months and 8 months of age.
source: Following plating at clonal density and 10 days of growth, 50–60% of CFU-F colonies derived from Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice exhibited relatively homogeneous tdTOMATO reporter expression while the other colonies were largely devoid of tdTOMATO positivity at both 2 months and 8 months of age (Figure 7a–c).
evidence: This is supported by CFU-F assay data shown in Figure 7a-c.

claim: 363 differentially expressed genes (227 enriched in tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs and 136 enriched in tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs) distinguished tdTOMATO+ from tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs.
source: Of the differentially expressed genes reaching significance (p < 0.05, LogFC >1), the three tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs clustered separately from three tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs on the basis of only 363 differentially expressed genes (227 enriched in tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs and 136 enriched in tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs) out of approximately 12,000 genes with an average expression level above biological thresholds (Figure 7d and Methods for threshold calculations).
evidence: This is supported by bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7d.

claim: Lepr, Grem1, Pdgfra, Adipoq, Pparg, Itgav, Cd200, and Cxcl12 were highly expressed in all CFU-Fs.
source: We observed Lepr, Grem1, Pdgfra, Adipoq, Pparg, Itgav, Cd200, and Cxcl12, all highly expressed above biological thresholds in all CFU-Fs, indicating a general maintenance of SSPC phenotype while in culture and a striking similarity between progenitors from disparate sources.
evidence: This is supported by bulk RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Gene ontology analysis identified 'cell population proliferation' and 'regulation of vascular development' as enriched in tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs.
source: To more readily identify differences between tdTOMATO+ and tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs, we performed gene ontology analysis for biological processes and found two interesting terms arise due to enriched expression of genes within the tdTOMATO+ or hypertrophic chondrocyte derived CFU-Fs; cell population proliferation and regulation of vascular development (Figure 7e; Mi et al., 2019; Gene Ontology Consortium, 2021; Ashburner et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis of bulk RNA-seq data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: A greater percentage of cells in tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs incorporated EdU compared to tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs at day 5 in culture.
source: To this end, we investigated EdU incorporation into all CFU-Fs from Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mice at day 5 in culture that consisted of at least 5 cells. We observed a greater percentage of cells in tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs that had incorporated EdU as compared to tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs (Figure 7f - top).
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 7f - top.

claim: By day 10 in culture, tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs were larger and displayed more colonies with 200+ cells compared to tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs.
source: By day 10 in culture, tdTOMATO+ CFU-Fs on average were larger and displayed more colonies with 200+ cells as compared to tdTOMATO- CFU-Fs (Figure 7f - bottom).
evidence: This is supported by colony size quantification data shown in Figure 7f - bottom.

claim: There was an equal or greater percentage of tdTOMATO+ SSPCs in a proliferative state (S, G2, or M phase) compared to osteoblasts in scRNA-seq data.
source: To determine whether this proliferative advantage could be observed in SSPCs immediately harvested from Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato bone marrow, we performed cell cycle analysis on our scRNA-seq dataset and found that as a percentage of the population there was an equal or greater percentage of tdTOMATO+ SSPCs (cluster 3, 4, and 5) in a proliferative state (S, G2, or M phase) as compared to osteoblasts (clusters 1 and 2) (Figure 7g).
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 7g.

claim: tdTOMATO+ and tdTOMATO- CFUs differentiated at similar capacities in vitro when measured by Alkaline Phosphatase, Von Kossa, and Oil Red O staining.
source: To determine whether tdTOMATO+ and tdTOMATO- CFUs contained inherent differences in their functional capacities to undergo osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation in vitro, we performed CFU-osteoblastic (CFU-Ob) and CFU-adipogenic (CFU-Ad) assays. Colonies composed of cells from either hypertrophic or non-hypertrophic origins were able to differentiate at similar capacities in vitro when measured by Alkaline Phosphatase, Von Kossa, and Oil Red O staining (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by CFU-Ob and CFU-Ad assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: tdTOMATO+ cells generated a full ossicle with bone marrow, vessels, and adipocytes in kidney capsule transplantations.
source: However, when we performed kidney capsule transplantations to generate bone ossicles in vivo, there was a much more apparent functional difference between tdTOMATO+ and tdTOMATO- cells. The tdTOMATO+ cells were able to generate a full ossicle with bone marrow, vessels, and adipocytes (Figure 8a -top and Figure 8b).
evidence: This is supported by kidney capsule transplantation data shown in Figure 8a and 8b.

claim: tdTOMATO- cells could only generate bone with no vascular invasion or adipocyte generation in kidney capsule transplantations.
source: Conversely, the tdTOMATO- cells could only generate bone with no vascular invasion or adipocyte generation (Figure 8 -bottom and Figure 8b).
evidence: This is supported by kidney capsule transplantation data shown in Figure 8a and 8b.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs are much more supportive of vascular invasion and marrow formation than SSPCs derived from other cell sources.
source: These apparent differences when transplanted suggest that hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs are much more supportive of vascular invasion and marrow formation than SSPCs derived from other cell sources.
evidence: This is inferred from the kidney capsule transplantation data showing differential outcomes.

claim: Current genetic lineage tracing studies have suggested a transdifferentiation mechanism by which hypertrophic chondrocytes differentiate directly into osteoprogenitors or mature osteoblasts.
source: Current genetic lineage tracing studies have suggested a transdifferentiation mechanism by which hypertrophic chondrocytes differentiate directly into an osteoprogenitor or mature osteoblast without transiting through an intermediate or more primitive state (Park et al., 2015).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as an existing hypothesis.

claim: This study provides genetic and transcriptomic evidence that hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo dedifferentiation to form SSPC populations.
source: Here, we have provided genetic and transcriptomic evidence, consistent with our hypothesis, that hypertrophic chondrocytes undergo a process of dedifferentiation to form SSPC populations ultimately giving rise to osteoblastic and adipogenic cell fates within the marrow compartment of embryonic, postnatal, and adult bones.
evidence: This is stated as the main conclusion of the study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocytes of the growth plate serve as a reservoir and alternative source of marrow-associated SSPCs utilized for rapid bone growth during skeletal development.
source: Our study demonstrates that hypertrophic chondrocytes of the growth plate serve as a reservoir and alternative source of marrow-associated SSPCs likely utilized for rapid bone growth during skeletal development (Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated as a main conclusion of the study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs expressing Pdgfra, Ly6a, Lepr, and Cxcl12 were identified at E16.5.
source: Specifically, our analyses of Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato and Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato skeletal rudiments at E16.5 identified not only hypertrophic chondrocytes (Col10a1 expressing cells) and their descendant osteoblasts (Bglap expressing cells), but also hypertrophic chondrocyte derived SSPCs expressing Pdgfra, Ly6a, Lepr, and Cxcl12.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis at E16.5.

claim: PαS cells (lineage negative, CXCL12-, PDGFRα+, SCA1+ SSPCs) are a quiescent population associated with vessels near the endosteum.
source: A population of lineage negative, CXCL12-, PDGFRα+, SCA1+ SSPCs (PαS cells) have been identified as a quiescent population associated with vessels near the endosteum (Morikawa et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge.

claim: PαS cells can form CFU-Fs, differentiate into osteoblasts, chondrocytes, and adipocytes, and are important for HSC migration and maintenance.
source: These PαS cells are also capable of forming CFU-Fs, can differentiate into osteoblasts, chondrocytes, and adipocytes, while also being important for the migration and maintenance of HSCs (Morikawa et al., 2009; Nusspaumer et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge.

claim: PαS-like cells derived from hypertrophic chondrocytes at E16.5 might be a transient population or of finite number that contribute early in development.
source: The appearance of these cells at E16.5 (but not 2 months) suggests that these might be either a more transient population derived from hypertrophic chondrocytes or are of an initial finite number and contribute early in development and are lost with age, as opposed to hypertrophic chondrocyte derived CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cells (Cxcl12+; Ly6a1-) that continue to be present in our data at 2 months of age.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential presence of Ly6a expression at E16.5 vs 2 months.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived CAR cells (Cxcl12+; Ly6a1-) continue to be present at 2 months of age.
source: The appearance of these cells at E16.5 (but not 2 months) suggests that these might be either a more transient population derived from hypertrophic chondrocytes or are of an initial finite number and contribute early in development and are lost with age, as opposed to hypertrophic chondrocyte derived CXCL12-abundant reticular (CAR) cells (Cxcl12+; Ly6a1-) that continue to be present in our data at 2 months of age.
evidence: This is stated based on the scRNA-seq data showing Cxcl12 expression at 2 months.

claim: Hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs/CAR cells were more proliferative than most primitive SSPC populations highlighted in other studies.
source: Interestingly, our scRNA-seq dataset identified similar proportions of cycling cells in hypertrophic chondrocyte derived SSPCs/CAR cells and osteoblasts. This is in stark contrast to the more quiescent phenotype observed in most primitive SSPC populations that have been highlighted across numerous studies (Tikhonova et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from cell cycle analysis of scRNA-seq data, contrasted with cited literature.

claim: Zhong et al. assessed proliferation rates of chondrocyte and perichondrial-derived SSPCs and osteoblasts in Col2a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato bone marrow and found similar proliferative capacities between later committed progenitors and osteoblasts.
source: However, recent work utilizing similar scRNA-seq approaches assessed proliferation rates of chondrocyte and perichondrial-derived SSPCs and osteoblast populations in the Col2a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato bone marrow and also indicated similar proliferative capacities between later committed progenitors and osteoblasts, which was greater than the most primitive of SSPCs (Zhong et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as supporting evidence.

claim: Zhong et al. found that AdipoqCreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato tdTOMATO+ cells contributed very little to CFU-Fs and exhibited minimal proliferation in vitro.
source: Zhong et al., also utilized the AdipoqCreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato model to investigate colony forming and proliferative potential of broad populations of Adipoq-expressing cells and descendants. These tdTOMATO+ cells contributed very little to CFU-Fs and exhibited minimal proliferation in vitro (Zhong et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as supporting evidence.

claim: Tikhonova et al. identified a subset of cells from the LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato lineage that cluster into a high cycling group using scRNA-seq.
source: Tikhonova et al. also utilized scRNA-seq and identified a subset of cells from the LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato lineage that cluster into a high cycling group (Tikhonova et al., 2019), which may represent a more proliferative LEPR+ SSPC population derived from the cartilage growth plate.
evidence: This is cited from prior literature with speculation about the origin of the high cycling group.

claim: The in vivo contribution of AdipoqCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato and LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato lineages to osteoblasts and/or osteocytes occurs over developmental time postnatally.
source: Finally, it is worth noting again that the in vivo contribution of AdipoqCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato and LeprCre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato lineages to osteoblasts and/or osteocytes is something that occurs over developmental time postnatally, while the Col10a1Cre; Rosa26fs-tdTomato lineage contributes to the osteoblast and osteocyte fates rapidly; as early as the embryonic period of skeletal development.
evidence: This is stated based on the immunofluorescence data comparing different Cre lines.

claim: The rapid contribution of Col10a1Cre lineage to osteoblasts may be attributed to the rapid or transient nature by which hypertrophic chondrocytes transit through the SSPC phase.
source: This may also be attributed to the rapid or transient nature by which hypertrophic chondrocytes transit through the SSPC phase during these periods, such that the LeprCre or AdipoqCre do not have sufficient time or levels of Cre expression to induce recombination within this population.
evidence: This is speculated as a possible explanation for the differential labeling kinetics.

claim: LeprCre and AdipoqCre may only be efficient at recombining floxed alleles within less transient SSPC populations postnatally.
source: Therefore, LeprCre and AdipoqCre may only be efficient at recombining floxed alleles within the less transient SSPC populations postnatally that continue to be maintained as SSPCs and subsequently slowly/weakly contribute to the osteogenic and adipogenic lineages during late postnatal/adult skeletal development and homeostasis.
evidence: This is speculated as a possible explanation for the differential labeling kinetics.

claim: WNT/β-catenin pathway has roles in balancing osteogenesis and adipogenesis from hypertrophic chondrocytes.
source: Recent publications have suggested roles for pathways like WNT/β-catenin in balancing osteogenesis and adipogenesis from hypertrophic chondrocytes (Tan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge.

claim: Sox9 is important for maintaining chondrocytes before changing fates toward the osteoblast lineage.
source: Additionally, Sox9 was shown to be important for maintaining chondrocytes before changing fates toward the osteoblast lineage (Haseeb et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge.

claim: Genetic deletion of Runx2 within hypertrophic chondrocytes initially reduces osteoblastic bone formation that ultimately fully recovers around 3-6 weeks of age.
source: Additional studies have also demonstrated a potential transient embryonic and postnatal contribution of hypertrophic chondrocytes to developmental bone formation, since genetic deletion of Runx2 within hypertrophic chondrocytes (and their descendants) initially reduces osteoblastic bone formation that ultimately fully recovers around 3–6 weeks of age (Qin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from prior literature as established knowledge.

claim: Removal of Runx2 within hypertrophic chondrocyte lineages may induce cell death, alter secreted factors, and/or delay re-differentiation of hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs.
source: While it is possible that the late postnatal formation is 'recovered' from osteoblasts derived purely from an alternate source (such as the periosteum), it is also possible that removal of Runx2 within the hypertrophic chondrocyte lineages induces some hypertrophic chondrocyte cell death, alters angiogenic/osteogenic factors (VEGFa among others) secreted from hypertrophic chondrocytes, and/or delays the re-differentiation of hypertrophic chondrocyte-derived SSPCs toward the osteoblast lineage; thus simply delaying postnatal bone formation by reducing the contribution of hypertrophic chondrocytes and their descendants to the earliest stages of bone development.
evidence: This is speculated as a possible alternative explanation for the Runx2 deletion phenotype.

claim: Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mouse line shows continued contribution of osteoblastic cells from hypertrophic chondrocytes throughout embryonic development to at least 4-5 months of age.
source: Further studies are needed to more thoroughly understand these lineage contributions over time, as we demonstrate with the Col10a1CreERT2; Rosa26fs-tdTomato mouse line that there is a continued contribution of osteoblastic cells from hypertrophic chondrocytes throughout embryonic development to at least approximately 4–5 months of age or skeletal maturity.
evidence: This is stated based on the lineage tracing data from Col10a1CreERT2 mice at different ages.
